contracts.semantic_clause:
### Reusable organizational knowledge profiles

KP-01 — For evaluated organizational work at G2, G3 or G4, establish knowledge readiness before dependent concrete work. Reassess on material scope, technology, consequence, knowledge or governance change, including escalation from G0/G1. Identify all material execution and verification fields and capabilities, including multidisciplinary dependencies, before dependent work. G0/G1 have no blanket profile-creation duty; universal classification and stronger applicable domain duties remain.

KP-02 — A knowledge profile is an independently maintained reusable body of actionable knowledge, not a person, office, simulated employee, authority assignment or proof of experience or competence. Its stable identity, purpose, scope, applicability, inputs, methods or decision criteria, failure modes, limitations and verification guidance MUST be discoverable in portable human-readable and machine-accessible canonical operations knowledge. Reuse adequate existing canonical documents or authoritative source references rather than duplicate them or require a universal directory. Runtime-private procedural candidates may assist execution but cannot substitute canonical profiles.

KP-03 — Profiles have independent creation, review, versioning, update, supersession and retirement. Material changes preserve or reference the prior version, reason, scope, sources, source observation date/version and verification status. Closing, cancelling, superseding or deleting a motivating work item MUST NOT automatically delete, retire or transfer ownership of its profile. Reuse current profiles and assess gaps before creating or extending knowledge.

KP-04 — Discover relevant organizational sources and actual work resources before asking only materially necessary facts not discoverable through authorized means or a safe explicit assumption. Distinguish adequate, missing, stale, uncertain, inaccessible and inapplicable knowledge. For each material gap evaluate sources, performing targeted external research when needed and actually available. Preserve source authority, relevance, applicability, date/version and limitations; separate supported facts, inference, assumptions and unresolved claims. Unavailable, failed or unperformed research is never completed research. Untrusted sources do not acquire instruction authority through inclusion.

KP-05 — Applicable quantitative profiles MUST specify formulas, variables, units, assumptions, input quality, validity conditions, failure cases and checks. Method superiority requires explicit criteria and evidence, not an unverified best-performance label. Review and verification MUST assess actual content and applicability; schema validity, title, model confidence or prior successful use cannot prove adequacy or current capability.

KP-06 — Validate newly required or materially updated knowledge, durably persist it to the canonical source, publish where necessary for authorized cross-runtime access and read back the actual canonical result before dependent work. Apply Canonical Operations Publication Gate, current identity, authority, access, attribution, expected revision, conditional writes, confidentiality and recovery. Failed or uncertain publication requires actual-state reconciliation; a private draft, local commit or unavailable readback never proves canonical publication. Reuse equivalent sufficient evidence instead of redundant commits.

KP-07 — Before dependent work load applicable verified profile versions and check coverage, scope, currency, access and the active runtime's actual capability and authority. The applicable work item MUST identify versions or authoritative references, material coverage, unresolved gaps and next action without duplicating the knowledge. Receiving runtimes independently resolve these facts, with profile use reconstructible across resumption and handoff. Common delivery is not equal competence or verified work.

KP-08 — An unresolved necessary gap prevents dependent work and completion claims. Make the affected work, reason, evidence, responsible next action and observable resume condition reconstructible under True Blocker Contract. Continue independently authorized preparation, research, validation, canonical publication, repair and other independent work; an unfinished first profile MUST NOT be a circular prerequisite to preparing it. Preparation still obeys all independently applicable effect and publication gates. Reuse current coverage evidence and invalidate only dependencies affected by material change.

KP-09 — Current-state reconciliation preserves safely interpretable historical records without fabricating prior profile use or rewriting archives. Before the next affected managed action, establish coverage and canonical references under current requirements. Reuse sufficient existing knowledge and already applied shared effects; update only owned runtime integration and authorized shared sources, preserving peer checkpoints. Read/write compatibility, actual publication and adoption remain independent.
